body.message: 01M3YH62V40012RJWKMGBKX3Q4 is completed_success and is not standing at a human gate. Approve, request changes and reject all answer `awaiting_review` and nothing else

body.name: bug
body.for_requests: Something that is broken: it used to work, or is meant to work, and does not, and what is wanted is the cause found and fixed. Taking a change that already landed back out whole is a revert, and adding or changing what the software does on purpose is a feature.

body.name: code_review
body.for_requests: A pull request somebody wants reviewed: a link to one, where the code is already written and what is wanted is a judgement on it rather than a change to it.

body.name: design_plan
body.for_requests: Working out how something should be built before anybody builds it: a design or plan drafted, then revised with whoever asked until they are content, where the result is a document and no code is written. Trying the idea out in code is a prototype.

body.name: epic
body.for_requests: Finishing a milestone or an epic: a link to one, or a list of issues somebody wants done as a whole, which is too much for one change and has to be split into several Jobs that run in turn.

body.name: feature
body.for_requests: Adding, removing or changing what the software does or shows: a new screen, option or command, a change to how something behaves, or taking away something people could see or use, meant to land and stay. Fixing something broken is a bug, and moving code around while nothing anyone sees changes is a refactor.

body.name: prototype
body.for_requests: Trying something out to answer a question: a spike or rough version built to see whether an idea works, shown to whoever asked and written up, then thrown away rather than landed. Something meant to ship is a feature, and a design worked out on paper is a design plan.

body.name: refactor
body.for_requests: Reorganising code without changing what it does: moving, renaming, splitting or tidying, where nothing anyone can see or use changes -- no screen, no output, no behaviour. A request that adds, removes or changes anything a person sees or can do, however small, is a feature and not a refactor.

body.name: revert
body.for_requests: Undoing a change that already landed: the commit or Job the request names, taken back out whole and nothing else with it. Keeping the change and fixing what it broke is a bug.
